stake_gate.note: stake 1: zf is this mask's pure aliasing with no prior, so it must read higher air energy than the reconstruction at every threshold -- if it did not, the air ratio would be blind to the very thing P4 asks about. stake 2: the uniform-mask positive control must show a more discrete PSF than the shipped blue-noise mask, or 'diffuse' is not being measured. A failure of either sends P4 to insufficient in adjudicate(); neither can create a true/false.

P4.reason: air-energy ratio_rec = ['2.317', '0.743', '0.398', '0.376'] across thresholds [0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04] (n_voxels [2484862, 6478311, 9204136, 9361668]). adjudicate() is blocked by these ratios alone: the `true` branch needs every ratio > 2.0 and the maximum here is 2.317; the `false` branch needs every |ratio - 1| < 0.2 and the worst is 1.317. The PSF term NEVER ENTERS the branch taken -- `diffuse` is read only inside the `false` branch, which the ratios already closed, so a perfectly diffuse PSF would change nothing. SEPARATE CONTEXT (not the blocking clause): psf_peak_sidelobe=0.1532 at the pre-registered mainlobe_radius=2, 0.0976 at r=3, against the uniform-mask positive control's 1.0000 (sidelobe_rms 0.0131 vs 0.0073) -- diffuse without needing any absolute constant. DIRECTION of the air reading: the ratio rises as the air threshold tightens for BOTH the reconstruction and the zero-fill reference (a selection effect -- air is defined by thresholding the GT, which shrinks the denominator without constraining the numerator), and the reconstruction sits below the zero-fill reference at every threshold (['7.510', '2.484', '1.377', '1.284']), i.e. the opposite of leakage.
P4.spec_literal_note: spec section 2 P4: 'true iff E_air(rec)/E_air(gt) >> 1 AND air-region error is same-family as zf's', with '>> 1' operationalised by the pre-registered rule as every point on the curve above 2.0. Measured: the curve sweeps from 2.317 at the tightest air threshold to 0.376 over the whole air mask, so it is not above 2 across the curve and the first conjunct fails -- which settles the conjunction whatever the second reads. The rise at the tightest threshold is a selection effect shared with the pure-aliasing reference, which sits ABOVE the reconstruction at every threshold (['7.510', '2.484', '1.377', '1.284']): there is no threshold at which the reconstruction puts more energy into air than zero-fill does. The implemented rule returns 'insufficient' rather than 'false' because the ratios are also not flat at 1. Spec section 1's own decision box reads this as 'the background grain is in the GT too -> section 8b stands'; nothing here overturns section 8b.

patchiness.run_to_run_noise_floor_note: |gauge-normalised selectivity(ctrlB) - gauge-normalised selectivity(shipped)|. ctrlB is the SAME acquisition, lambda and iteration count as the shipped run with only a different AF=12 mask draw, so this is what 'no change in patchiness' measures as on this index. Compare it against the two arms' deltas before reading either as a signal: a delta smaller than this floor is not distinguishable from a re-draw.
patchiness.gauge_normalization_provenance: POST-HOC: dividing each arm's selectivity by its OWN zf anchor was introduced at fix round 1 (2026-08-11), after the raw comparison had already been computed. It is defensible (memory.md section 3's metric-gauge trap: each arm is a different acquisition, so their anchors are not interchangeable), but its DIRECTION OF EFFECT IS DATA-DEPENDENT, NOT conservative by construction -- it can CREATE an attribution the raw arms did not support just as readily as it can remove one. On this run (contrast=FLAIR) it CREATED an attribution the raw comparison did not support: raw deltas +0.0718/-0.0698 -> raw_agree=False; gauge-normalised deltas +0.3101/+0.1309 -> agree=True. It was NOT pre-registered and is recorded as such here rather than only in a session log.
